Meanwhile, Cammy is in Dumfrieshire to meet a young dairy farmer who got her big break into the industry via a unique opportunity.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Coverage of the Group C match between Haiti and Scotland from Boston Stadium. Scotland play their first game at a World Cup in 28 years, as Steve Clarke’s team seek a winning start with matches still to come against Morocco and Brazil, who they met in the first game of their last campaign back in 1998. They sealed qualification in dramatic fashion by beating Denmark at Hampden Park last November and will be backed by huge numbers of the Tartan Army in Boston, who will be hoping for a better showing than at Euro 2024, when they exited with just one point from the group stage. Haiti have had to wait even longer for World Cup football, having qualified for their second ever tournament, last making an appearance in 1974, when they were knocked out in the first round following defeats to Italy, Poland and Argentina. They are managed by French coach Sebastien Migne, and their squad includes Wolves midfielder Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up an array of delicious dishes from some favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Theo Randall kicks things off with tagliarini served with red mullet, tomatoes, olives and pangrattato. Ching-He Huang prepares an effortless three-cup chicken with cauliflower fried rice and chilli sauce rice. Georgina Hayden delivers some Greek sunshine to the studio with her kreatopitas, Marianne Lumb gives mille-feuille a savoury makeover alongside a tomato consommé, and Matt Adlard prepares his elevated choc ices. Finally, Angela Scanlon tucks into either her food heaven, miso braised mushrooms with roasted scallops, or her food hell, lamb stew with chilli and lemon gremolata. Meanwhile, Rick Stein heads to Glastonbury to rock out at a beef farm, and the Hairy Bikers make ‘nduja in Italy.

programme.title: Strangers on a Train
programme.desc: Alfred Hitchcock's suspense classic about two men who plot a perfect murder. When tennis pro Guy Haines meets smooth-talking Bruno Antony in the bar of a train, he finds the stranger sympathetic with his desire to be rid of his clinging wife. The sinister Bruno then proposes that they swap murders: Bruno will murder Guy's wife, and Guy will do away with Bruno's father. From Patricia Highsmith's novel.

programme.title: Dial M for Murder
programme.desc: Margot Wendice tells her former lover, Mark, that her husband, Tony, has turned over a new leaf and is loving and attentive. While Margot is worrying about a stolen love letter, Tony has devised the perfect murder. Alfred Hitchcock's famed drama of deadly intrigue and dogged detective work.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: A retrospective look at television appearances made over the years by iconic Hollywood director Alfred Hitchcock, reflecting on the milestones and highlights of his life and career. Narrated by Sylvia Syms.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Members of the public try and make money out of their antiques.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Filmed across a year, this series follows the lives of five farming families across Scotland. The autumn sales are over, and preparations are being made for winter. In Newtonmore, in the Cairngorms National Park, Robert MacKenzie needs to gather in all his pregnant cows back to the croft for pregnancy testing. Costs of feed and fertiliser have shot up this year, so if not enough are in calf, it may be time to stop farming cattle. In North Uist, the MacDonald family are harvesting potatoes grown in the sandy Machair soil that is unique to the west of Scotland. The croft has been in Angus’s hands since the 1980s, but now he is steadily handing over the reins to son Fraser and daughter-in-law Carianne. On Thorabella Farm in Moray, Nikki and Ollie Lake are doing things a bit differently, having bought their first farm in 2017 with the goal of living as self-sufficiently as possible. They need to call on the vet to help one of their cows that is experiencing a difficult birth.

programme.title: Expedition Killer Whale
programme.desc: In Antarctica, the most sophisticated hunting behaviour in the animal kingdom takes place – killer whales creating waves to wash seals off pieces of floating ice. A team of scientists and filmmakers travel to these freezing waters to find out more about these unique animals and how they do it. And one of the scientists is looking for one killer whale in particular. But their mission is not just to deepen our understanding of this extraordinary hunting behaviour. The team are also intent on learning more about the secret – and more tender side – of the lives of these killer whales.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From the conservation of an apprentice indenture from 1785 that tied a 13-year-old boy to a cotton mill, to the unusual homes of working families at Kinver Edge carved into a sandstone hillside, this episode uncovers the hidden lives of ordinary working people – and follows the teams making sure their stories are never forgotten.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Naturalist Steve Backshall and a team of dive experts embark on an expedition to the eastern Pacific Ocean. Steve joins forces with renowned shark scientist Mauricio Hoyos to dive the largest marine protected area in North America – the Revillagigedo National Park in Mexico. Here, they hope to witness some of the richest marine life on the planet – whale sharks, Galapagos sharks, hammerhead sharks and giant manta rays are known to gather here in huge numbers. From the Baja Peninsula in Mexico, the team travels over 700km into the open ocean. Their goal is to dive unexplored areas around the remote volcanic island of Clarion to discover whether this might be a shark nursery. Shark populations are crashing globally, as they are targeted by the illegal shark fin trade. Sharks are slow breeders – some species only have a few young at a time, and they take a long time to reach maturity. When commercial fishing boats catch one shark, it’s not just one life lost – it can be a whole generation. If Steve and Mauricio can discover where shark mothers give birth, they can help protect a new generation of these ocean giants.

programme.title: The Mother of All Cons
programme.desc: Megan has tragically died. Her friends are devastated, as is the entire Believe in Magic community. But, on the day of her funeral, the service is suddenly cancelled. The authorities want to carry out another autopsy, and rumours circulate that the police are now involved. The sleuths ask: if Megan didn’t have a brain tumour, how did she die? Megan’s older half-sister Nina has long doubted the diagnosis and is equally confused by her sudden death. Soon, a coroner's inquest concludes Megan died of natural causes - cardiac arrhythmia caused by fatty liver disease. Crucially, there is no mention of a brain tumour, and her brain is described as 'morphologically normal'. The sleuths feel vindicated. But some of Megan’s closest friends are baffled. If Megan wasn’t ill, why did she show symptoms? And why was she taking such enormous quantities of medication? Nina suspects their mother, Jean, knows more, and she begins a search for an answer.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: With Lola Young, Mike D 5D, Baby Rose, Wasia Project, Beverly Glenn-Copeland and Elizabeth Copeland, and Bonnie 'Prince' Billy.

programme.title: Children of Men
programme.desc: 2027. In a chaotic future, children are no longer being born because of a years-long fertility crisis. Borders are closed, and Britain has become a brutal police state, with immigrants herded into cages and treated like animals. Government employee Theo receives a message from someone from his past, asking for help getting a refugee some papers. But Theo is soon drawn into something much bigger than himself. Kee is not just a refugee needing help - she is pregnant.

If Steve and Mauricio can discover where shark mothers give birth, they can help protect a new generation of these ocean giants.

programme.title: The Mother of All Cons
programme.desc: Megan has tragically died. Her friends are devastated, as is the entire Believe in Magic community. But, on the day of her funeral, the service is suddenly cancelled. The authorities want to carry out another autopsy, and rumours circulate that the police are now involved. The sleuths ask: if Megan didn’t have a brain tumour, how did she die? Megan’s older half-sister Nina has long doubted the diagnosis and is equally confused by her sudden death. Soon, a coroner's inquest concludes Megan died of natural causes - cardiac arrhythmia caused by fatty liver disease. Crucially, there is no mention of a brain tumour, and her brain is described as 'morphologically normal'. The sleuths feel vindicated. But some of Megan’s closest friends are baffled. If Megan wasn’t ill, why did she show symptoms? And why was she taking such enormous quantities of medication? Nina suspects their mother, Jean, knows more, and she begins a search for an answer.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Coverage of the Group C match between Haiti and Scotland from Boston Stadium. Scotland play their first game at a World Cup in 28 years, as Steve Clarke’s team seek a winning start with matches still to come against Morocco and Brazil, who they met in the first game of their last campaign back in 1998. They sealed qualification in dramatic fashion by beating Denmark at Hampden Park last November and will be backed by huge numbers of the Tartan Army in Boston, who will be hoping for a better showing than at Euro 2024, when they exited with just one point from the group stage. Haiti have had to wait even longer for World Cup football, having qualified for their second ever tournament, last making an appearance in 1974, when they were knocked out in the first round following defeats to Italy, Poland and Argentina. They are managed by French coach Sebastien Migne, and their squad includes Wolves midfielder Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up an array of delicious dishes from some favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Theo Randall kicks things off with tagliarini served with red mullet, tomatoes, olives and pangrattato. Ching-He Huang prepares an effortless three-cup chicken with cauliflower fried rice and chilli sauce rice. Georgina Hayden delivers some Greek sunshine to the studio with her kreatopitas, Marianne Lumb gives mille-feuille a savoury makeover alongside a tomato consommé, and Matt Adlard prepares his elevated choc ices. Finally, Angela Scanlon tucks into either her food heaven, miso braised mushrooms with roasted scallops, or her food hell, lamb stew with chilli and lemon gremolata. Meanwhile, Rick Stein heads to Glastonbury to rock out at a beef farm, and the Hairy Bikers make ‘nduja in Italy.

programme.title: Strangers on a Train
programme.desc: Alfred Hitchcock's suspense classic about two men who plot a perfect murder. When tennis pro Guy Haines meets smooth-talking Bruno Antony in the bar of a train, he finds the stranger sympathetic with his desire to be rid of his clinging wife. The sinister Bruno then proposes that they swap murders: Bruno will murder Guy's wife, and Guy will do away with Bruno's father. From Patricia Highsmith's novel.

programme.title: Dial M for Murder
programme.desc: Margot Wendice tells her former lover, Mark, that her husband, Tony, has turned over a new leaf and is loving and attentive. While Margot is worrying about a stolen love letter, Tony has devised the perfect murder. Alfred Hitchcock's famed drama of deadly intrigue and dogged detective work.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: A retrospective look at television appearances made over the years by iconic Hollywood director Alfred Hitchcock, reflecting on the milestones and highlights of his life and career. Narrated by Sylvia Syms.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: The final episode in the series, and Derek Brockway, the weatherman, veers off the Wales coast path to walk along a section of the stunning Mawddach trail near Barmouth. He takes an early morning canoe trip and hears a story of incredible bravery. On this walk he also visits the village of Fairbourne, and takes a ride on its special small-scale train. Archaeologist Dr Erin Lloyd-Jones goes in search of local gold and Matt Bassett goes star-gazing… but is defeated by the Welsh weather.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from the Bowes Museum at Barnard Castle in County Durham. The museum was purpose-built to house the collection of Josephine and John Bowes, and in the picture galleries experts Elizabeth Talbot and Paul Laidlaw pick out some gems to value; among them are prints depicting the first steeple-chase on record and an intriguing carved coconut.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Filmed across a year, this series follows the lives of five farming families across Scotland. The autumn sales are over, and preparations are being made for winter. In Newtonmore, in the Cairngorms National Park, Robert MacKenzie needs to gather in all his pregnant cows back to the croft for pregnancy testing. Costs of feed and fertiliser have shot up this year, so if not enough are in calf, it may be time to stop farming cattle. In North Uist, the MacDonald family are harvesting potatoes grown in the sandy Machair soil that is unique to the west of Scotland. The croft has been in Angus’s hands since the 1980s, but now he is steadily handing over the reins to son Fraser and daughter-in-law Carianne. On Thorabella Farm in Moray, Nikki and Ollie Lake are doing things a bit differently, having bought their first farm in 2017 with the goal of living as self-sufficiently as possible. They need to call on the vet to help one of their cows that is experiencing a difficult birth.

programme.title: Expedition Killer Whale
programme.desc: In Antarctica, the most sophisticated hunting behaviour in the animal kingdom takes place – killer whales creating waves to wash seals off pieces of floating ice. A team of scientists and filmmakers travel to these freezing waters to find out more about these unique animals and how they do it. And one of the scientists is looking for one killer whale in particular. But their mission is not just to deepen our understanding of this extraordinary hunting behaviour. The team are also intent on learning more about the secret – and more tender side – of the lives of these killer whales.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From the conservation of an apprentice indenture from 1785 that tied a 13-year-old boy to a cotton mill, to the unusual homes of working families at Kinver Edge carved into a sandstone hillside, this episode uncovers the hidden lives of ordinary working people – and follows the teams making sure their stories are never forgotten.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Naturalist Steve Backshall and a team of dive experts embark on an expedition to the eastern Pacific Ocean. Steve joins forces with renowned shark scientist Mauricio Hoyos to dive the largest marine protected area in North America – the Revillagigedo National Park in Mexico. Here, they hope to witness some of the richest marine life on the planet – whale sharks, Galapagos sharks, hammerhead sharks and giant manta rays are known to gather here in huge numbers. From the Baja Peninsula in Mexico, the team travels over 700km into the open ocean. programme.desc: Rebecca is keen to go on a travelling adventure and invites Murphi to come. Murphi’s time machine takes them to the dinosaur age, but when it stops working, they need to get making. Firstly, they create a paper plate dinosaur, followed by some colourful water blob creatures made by the Mini Monsters. Then, Rebecca gets a call on the Magic Monster Mirror from her aunt Antarctic, who makes herself some snow-building buddies to help rescue her snowman. The Recycling Express brings some paper straws to the attic, which Murphi and Rebecca use to make a straw sailboat.

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Jen’s being really clumsy in the cafe and can’t work out why. Asteroid the alien comes to visit, Small flies off to see how apples grow, and the cooks make wobbly space jelly for their intergalactic guest.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to a place where they’ll make a nature collage using leaves and sticks. On the way, they discover a chocolate river and a bridge that looks like a sheep, choo-choo like an old train and even meet a dragon!

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: On Big Fix Day, Ava’s Good-As-New machine repairs everything - even things that don’t need mending. But when it fails, she has to find another way to fix the children’s toys.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee and the Squirrels take their teddy bears out for a picnic. But hang on - who does that huge teddy belong to? Oh! That's not a teddy at all! It's Beryl, and she's a real bear! She wants to join in the fun but has no teddy of her own, so the Squirrels make her one using sticks, leaves, acorns... and a big pink sock! Now Beryl can join the picnic with everyone else.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. When Shellington and the crew try to gather some skittish crabs who have drifted away from home, they get help from some old friends.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Toby the gopher has trouble catching a ball, and doing pretty much everything else, Vida gives him an eye exam and learns he can’t see very well. Luckily, she knows just what to do, and soon his sight is perfect - and he has a cool new pair of glasses!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters are adventure-seeking explorers who soar around the planet fixing environmental problems caused by Grandmaster Glitch!

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi spots an old family photo, where she looks small next to her dads. Wanting to seem more grown up, she wishes to be taller - and suddenly she is! It’s fun at first, but she soon realises she misses being carried by her dads and the closeness of doing things together.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Toad finds himself with a case of puddle hiccups, it’s up to Yukee and the rest of the garden gang to find a cure.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets enjoy a fin-tastic fishing adventure and end up with an unexpected catch.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Mr Tumble gets in a muddle while helping Grandad Tumble look after the garden. Justin meets Ryan, his new friend, in a walled garden to help take care of the plants. George joins them to do some watering. There's a decorative recycling spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words seeds, garden and plant.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Ava’s solar gadgets malfunction, making her doubt her skills. But with PC Plum’s encouragement, she realises that each invention needs a different-sized solar panel.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Peas encounter a pack of Radishraptors who steal their delicious pop drops!

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Heritage seed expert Lucy and the Fact Pack explore the colourful world of heritage tomatoes and discover why eating different-coloured fruits and vegetables is good for us.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Iona and Elba create a pretend ice cream shop and make Mum a heart-shaped ice cream cake. Then it’s time for some real ice cream with plenty of sprinkles for decoration. On a family walk in the woods, Iona and Elba discover a trail of fairy clues to follow. They find fairy treats and magic wands, but will the spells they cast work on Mum and Dad?

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Myrtle wants to practise her newly learned first aid skills.

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers are a team of five friends on an interstellar journey to explore fantastic planets, with the aim of learning about and playing new games. The discovered games are collected into a database to make sure they are never lost.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Five wishes to fly up to the stars, but she doesn’t have enough blocks to get there. She tries adding different Numberblock friends, but no-one can make her tall enough to reach the sky. Can Five figure out what she needs to reach the stars and make a wish?

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Imaginative Purple arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour purple.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca is trying to win a lasso contest, but first, there’s some making to be done with Murphi. A toothpaste box and a toothpaste tube are transformed into a toothpaste tube snake, the Mini Monsters create something beastly out of burger boxes, and Rebecca’s cousin calls on the Magic Monster Mirror. Finally, a large cardboard tube provides inspiration for a terrific tube vulture.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button use kitchen foil to create and launch an out-of-this-world spaceship.

programme.title: Get Set Galactic
programme.desc: Two teams take on three scientific challenges based on floating or sinking, fossils and forces. James’s shoes are slippy, but Ayo and Sam help find a solution with a moon buggy!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children play with rubber ducks, learning BSL signs for ducks, far away and swimming, then sing and sign Five Little Ducks Went Swimming One Day.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick is having a busy day when a very tired bee visits him and Norman in the caravan. Together with the Popcasters, they learn how important bees are to the planet, and they write a song to help the busy bee get its buzz back.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Sunny doesn’t want to see the Sweetwood Band, even though he loves music, Vida helps him out with earmuffs and he gets to enjoy the show!

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Twiggy has a funny tummy on the day of his performance. Nothing the doctors try works, not even the cure for froggy moths! Zog wonders if there is something else bothering Twiggy.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Ruby and Finn’s seeds have started to grow, but Rafi’s cherry seed shows no change. Feeling left out, she makes a wish, and a giant cherry tree appears! It’s exciting at first, but when the wish ends, everything disappears. Rafi feels sad, until Doris shares a story about planting an apple tree when she was little. Rafi realises that nature likes to take its time and waiting can bring something special.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo must prove Mr Monkeyjocks is special to save him from being chucked out.

programme.title: Nikhil & Jay
programme.desc: Nikhil, Jay and their family celebrate Deepavali, also known as Diwali, with kolam, laddus and bunting. But will they be able to watch the fireworks without scaring Max the cat?

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Flamingo and John give Sarah and Duck a tour of their house and invite them to play their favourite game.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Lola wants the bedroom door open, the window blind up and the light on after she hears the story of an ogre. Charlie tries to rid his sister of her fears by reading the end of the story book, revealing a happy ending with the ogre. Lola then insists on having the light off because she and her friendly ogre can't possibly sleep unless it is totally dark!

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: A relaxing, magical show about a lovely group of handmade toys who come to life at night. Join Pepi Nana and Moon Baby on their gentle adventures to the land of stories.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo loves jumping, but BaBa is struggling to jump like MeMo. At the Play Tree, they play with a jumpy planet that can jump very high. On the Lullaby Lake, Fungi and Pungi jump out of the water to greet MeMo and BaBa as they make their way to Gramma Leeba in the Bay of Books.

programme.desc: Series for young children about a magical place inhabited by a community of toy characters that care for each other and have fun together. Finally, the teeny-tiny Pontipines board, but they are so small that nobody notices them arrive.

From Greek chicken gyros to mozzarella panzanella with a fruity twist, these recipes are perfect for those long, lazy days and holiday get-togethers! Lisa Snowdon pops in to make her summertime favourite seafood linguine, and chef Joseph Denison Carey goes strawberry picking in the sun.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined in her kitchen by Michelin-starred chef Tom Kerridge as he cooks smoky beef and short ribs which can also be cooked on a barbecue - Tom also talks about when he first started cooking as a boy and how that set him on course to become a successful chef, but he then has an accident while making a sauce with a food mixer that leaves him covered in food. Prue then makes chicken tikka with a kachumber salad while John heads off to Larkhill Vineyard to pick up some tips on becoming a successful wine producer - Prue's food hero this time is Moch Coch, a charcuterie in west Wales run by Bethan, who used to be an acupuncturist but now runs a pig farm. Finally, John joins Prue in the kitchen to prepare an impressive cheese and chutney board with a duck rillette while Prue has a mouthwatering hack for garlic confit which can be stored in a jar and has many uses.

The pair end their day with a treat as Barney has arranged an exclusive and unique dinner. The next day the boys head out of the city towards the beautiful Blue Mountains, famed for its spectacular scenery, but once again, Brad's fear of heights is put to the test when they take a ride on what turns out to be an extreme cable car.

programme.title: Bradley & Barney Walsh: Breaking Dad
programme.desc: The new series continues as Bradley and Barney are well into their Australian road trip, and before they leave the beautiful Blue Mountains, Barney has an extreme challenge planned for his dad as they must traverse a ravine on a rope! The boys then head into the countryside and make a stop in the land of sheep, where they learn the art of shearing. Their road trip then takes them to a tiny town where they join the local community who've organised a mighty challenge that involves pulling a gigantic truck.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined in her kitchen by Michelin-starred chef Tom Kerridge as he cooks smoky beef and short ribs which can also be cooked on a barbecue - Tom also talks about when he first started cooking as a boy and how that set him on course to become a successful chef, but he then has an accident while making a sauce with a food mixer that leaves him covered in food. Prue then makes chicken tikka with a kachumber salad while John heads off to Larkhill Vineyard to pick up some tips on becoming a successful wine producer - Prue's food hero this time is Moch Coch, a charcuterie in west Wales run by Bethan, who used to be an acupuncturist but now runs a pig farm. Finally, John joins Prue in the kitchen to prepare an impressive cheese and chutney board with a duck rillette while Prue has a mouthwatering hack for garlic confit which can be stored in a jar and has many uses.

Prue then makes chicken tikka with a kachumber salad while John heads off to Larkhill Vineyard to pick up some tips on becoming a successful wine producer - Prue's food hero this time is Moch Coch, a charcuterie in west Wales run by Bethan, who used to be an acupuncturist but now runs a pig farm. Finally, John joins Prue in the kitchen to prepare an impressive cheese and chutney board with a duck rillette while Prue has a mouthwatering hack for garlic confit which can be stored in a jar and has many uses.

programme.desc: Napoleonic War-based action-adventure. June 1813 - the South Essex is seriously short of men, and when the Duke of Wellington is told that there are no recruits available, he sends Sharpe to England to investigate. When Sharpe and Harper arrive, they are informed that there are 700 men waiting for them in Chelmsford - however, Sharpe finds the barracks deserted with no sign of his missing regiment. He and Harper decide to assume other identities and enlist - recruited by Sergeant Havercamp, Sharpe and Harper arrive at a training camp near the estate of Sir Henry Simmerson where they are trained mercilessly. Sharpe discovers that the new recruits are being auctioned to other regiments and returns to the Horse Guards with this information to entrust it to an old friend called Lawford... but Lawford wants to avoid a scandal and promptly tells Lord Fenner, who tries to have Sharpe killed. programme.title: Sharpe
programme.desc: Napoleonic War-based action-adventure. Winter 1813 - Wellington is informed by the debonair Comte de Maquerre that Bordeaux is ready to rebel against Napoleon, but Wellington's spymaster Ross is suspicious and tests Maquerre by suggesting that they use Maquerre's own castle as a base. Maquerre reluctantly agrees but says that the castle is in Napoleon's hands, so Wellington appoints Colonel Bampfylde to lead the attack on the castle with Sharpe in support. Bampfylde, who is intent on glory, sends Sharpe on a scouting mission and tries to capture the castle on his own, but he fails and casualties are heavy - Sharpe, who is a witness to the carnage, therefore has Harris and Frederickson sneak into the castle in disguise, and they soon force the French to surrender once inside. Ashamed by Sharpe's victory, Bampfylde sends him off on a reconnaissance mission - however, Sharpe soon discovers that Bordeaux has no intention of rising against Napoleon and that Maquerre is a double agent.
